title: Thought about David Moss at the end of Glengarry Glen Ross

commenti.body: You got the memory of a fuckin fly. Moss is disillusioned because he knows the Glengarry leads they stole are just a bunch of fucking deadbeats, just like the leads they already had. They're selling their customers worthless land, and they're being sold worthless leads by Alec Baldwin.

I'd always thought his rant was just keeping up the pretense that he was innocent and salty about being grilled by the cops. It would be odd for him to break from being angry to speak to Levene. He didn't need to try and keep Levene sweet because he knew Levene wouldn't rat him out to the cops because he'd be implicating himself too.

I know Moss is kinda dumb, but it's far more sensible for him to act pissed off after coming out of the interrogation (which he does) and then quietly go over to Graff, which was his plan all along. Everything should be peach fuzz for him, he's got an alliby, 5000 bucks and a new job. For him to yell at Levene who is yet to go in the room and could panic and blow everything to me makes no sense unless you add some extra factor for him like him not getting a job with Graff, then he's just got 5000 in his pocket. BIG DEAL!
Okay so I've seen this movie at least a dozen times, and I never picked up on the fact that the Glengarry leads were dogshit.

It's not explicitly stated that the leads are dogshit, but it makes sense. They also never actually show you the worthless land that they are selling, you just know it's worthless because they are con men.

Yeah, I didn't think it was stated, but it does make sense. It was already established that Moss was an aggressive, immature man with a victim complex -- I figured the next morning was just an extension of that. But the context of the leads being awful *after* he stole him fits perfectly.

I guess I will be watching it again soon.
